deep.reconstruction:
The page has two layers.

(1) Typed English paragraph (rotated, left margin). This is evidently a page from the 1983 English typescript of the Pursuing Stacks period, reused as scratch paper. Fragment: "B = (Gr-stacks), B^, B(0)^ ... commutes not only with arbitrary projective limits, but equally with arbitrary direct limits, or what amounts to the same, that direct limits in the category (Gr-stacks) can be computed component-wise. (Here B(0) stands for the full subcategory of B formed by the basic objects D_n, n in N.)"
- Gr-stacks are Grothendieck's weak infinity-groupoids.
- B(0) is the full subcategory of the globular 'discs' D_n.
- The functor B -> B(0)^ sends an infinity-groupoid to its underlying globular set (F_n = Hom(D_n, F)).
- The sentence asserts, or more likely discusses as a desideratum (the beginning of the sentence is missing), that this functor preserves all colimits.

(2) Handwritten French notes, scratch for the next page (p.6). There Grothendieck abstracts a 'category of models' M with two properties: (i) every arrow is a monomorphism; (ii) every endomorphism is the identity.
- For each object D, D~ is the poset of subobjects of D.
- Hom(D', D) -> D~, u |-> u(D'), is injective. Its image Phi_{D'}(D) is the set of subobjects isomorphic to D'.
- N, the set of isomorphism classes, is ordered. One gets a family n |-> D~_n of posets indexed by the poset I = N.
- Each D~_n carries a strictly increasing map k_n : D~_n -> I (the 'type' of a subobject), with image I_{<=n}.
- For n' <= n, Phi_{n';n} = {x in D~_n | k_n(x) = n'}, which is identified with Hom(D_{n'}, D_n).
- Maps D~_{n'} -> D~_n are drawn. The configuration x'' < x' in D~_n, y'' < y', of types n'' and n', is about composing face inclusions, i.e. recovering the composition of M from the posets.

The count 1 + n*2 + C(n,2)*2^2 + ... + 2^n = (1+2)^n = 3^n is the number of nonempty faces of the n-cube. A face of codimension k can be chosen in C(n,k)*2^k ways. So the test example is the semi-cubical category (face inclusions of cubes): D~_n is the face poset of the n-cube.

The remaining jottings tie this back to the globular/Gr-stack setting of p.4:
- the globular set F_0 <= F_1 <= F_2 (double arrows);
- a loop at x, with 'pi(F_*, x) = ensemble des classes d'homotopie de lacets en x' (really pi_1, written pi_0 of the loop object);
- a rotated marginal formula equating a projective limit of the D~_n with a limit of Sigma_n (illegible, possibly symmetric groups or the cube's automorphisms).

Purpose: to set up a general combinatorial framework of 'direct' model categories, in which a model category is encoded by the posets of subobjects of its objects. Presheaves on it (generalized semi-simplicial, semi-cubical or globular complexes) can then be handled uniformly. The setting is the comparison of Gr-stacks with globular sets and the homotopy invariants pi_i and lifting criteria of the previous page.
errors: The typed claim that the functor (Gr-stacks) -> globular sets preserves arbitrary direct limits, i.e. that colimits of infinity-groupoids are computed componentwise, is false as stated. Forgetful functors from algebraic structures preserve filtered colimits but not pushouts or coequalizers in general; already for ordinary groupoids, pushouts are not computed on underlying graphs. Since the start of the sentence is cut off, the typescript may be stating what one would like, or denying it.
'pi_0(F_*, x) = classes d'homotopie de lacets en x' should be pi_1(F, x), or pi_0 of the loop space; this is a notational slip.

ideas.what: Underlying globular set functor from infinity-groupoids (Gr-stacks) to presheaves on the globe category B(0), and its exactness properties (limits/colimits)
ideas.modern_name: Forgetful functor from Grothendieck (weak) infinity-groupoids to globular sets; monadicity/accessibility
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, 1983); formalized by Maltsiniotis (2010), Ara
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983, published 2021 SMF Documents Mathématiques), discussion of Gr-stacks and coherators

ideas.what: Category of models M in which all arrows are monic and all endomorphisms are identities; encoding Hom(D',D) by the subobject poset D~ with a type map k_n : D~_n -> I_{<=n}
ideas.modern_name: Direct category (skeletal, mono-only Reedy category); face-poset description, cf. regular/Eilenberg–Zilber categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Reedy (1974), Kan; direct categories in Hovey's model category theory; Berger–Moerdijk (EZ categories)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related passages in Pursuing Stacks on categories of models and test categories; unsure

ideas.what: Face count of the n-cube: sum_k C(n,k) 2^k = 3^n, used to identify D~_n as the cube's face poset
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of the n-cube / semi-cubical sets

ideas.what: Homotopy classes of loops at a base point of a globular set / Gr-stack
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; Grothendieck in Pursuing Stacks for Gr-stacks

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins axiomatizing direct ('mono-only, no nontrivial endomorphisms') model categories via the indexed family of subobject posets (D~_n, k_n). The aim seems to be reconstructing composition in M from these posets, so that globular, semi-cubical and semi-simplicial shapes can be treated uniformly. The thread on p.6 starts this but it does not appear to be developed in Pursuing Stacks as such.
missed.quote: n |-> D~_n famille d'un ordonné, D~_n --k_n--> I str. crois. image I_{<=n} ... Soit Phi_{n';n} ⊂ D~_n = {x ∈ D~_n | k_n(x) = n'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is close to modern characterizations of direct and regular Reedy categories by face posets. It is of mild interest as an early independent formulation, but the substance is known.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly scratch work on known Pursuing Stacks themes: Gr-stacks over globular sets, the cube face count, and direct categories of models. The poset encoding of a direct model category is a small unpublished detail, but it is conceptually standard today.
transcription_corrections: The typed English text is a rotated Pursuing Stacks-era typescript page underlying the handwriting (paper reuse), not part of the French notes.
'x'' < x' ∈ D_n' should be '∈ D~_n'. The diagram shows x'' < x' and y'' < y' with types n'' and n', separated by a curved line.
'pi_0(F_x, x)' is likely 'pi(F_*, x)' (or pi_1) = ensemble des classes d'homotopie de lacets en x.
The rotated right-margin formula ('lim D~_n = lim Sigma_n') is largely illegible; the transcription is uncertain.
'image ⊂ I' should read 'image ⊂ I_{<=n}' (the crossed-out N was replaced by I).
